Every factual claim below was re-measured in this run against the files in this checkout, and the two rejection objections were reproduced before being fixed. The ten `it('...')` titles extracted from each file are identical, ten lines each. Diffing the two describe blocks (`sed -n '181,338p'` against `sed -n '380,549p'`) returns 76 changed lines; filtering those 76 lines for `expect|toEqual|toBe|toHave` returns zero. Every hunk is the props wrapper alone, `runCustom({...})` against `runCustom(weeklyProps({...}))`. The 7/3 split holds in both files. The weeklyRows fixture is byte-identical (md5 6342ab83b4f60f70b3f77d129ec0d601 in both). weeklyProps supplies precisely the defaults the shorter file's own runCustom already defaulted to, plus `balanceTypeOp: undefined`, which sortData.ts:24 already guards with `if (!balanceTypeOp || !sortByOp) return () => 0`. A repo-wide grep for 'weekly-end-date' returns no hit in any source, config or CI file, and vitest discovers tests by the glob at vite.config.mts:406, so nothing has to be unlisted along with the deletion.

validated_work_order.debate_summary: v3 was rejected on two objections, both the same failure mode as v1 and v2: two artefacts in one work order could not both be satisfied. (1) AC-2.how_to_verify required the mandated comment's 'fourth line' to name weekly-end-date.test.ts, but in the block files[1] quotes the token is on the third line — reproduced here by printing the 13 lines with indices. An implementer inserting files[1]'s block verbatim, which AC-2 also demands character for character, could not satisfy AC-2. Only AC-2's ordinal was wrong; check, files[1] and step 6 described the block correctly. Fixed in AC-2 alone, to 'third line', exactly as the reviewer required — files[1]'s block is not edited to chase the ordinal, since it is the artefact AC-2 is judged against. files[1] now also states the block's line count, its first and last lines, and that the token is on line 3, so the two artefacts carry the same facts in one edit. (2) qa_script step 3's grep could not print nothing at QA time: the pipeline writes a pretty-printed work-order.json into the repo root (sdlc-qa.yml:154 → fetch-work-order.mjs → JSON.stringify(wo, null, 2)), and step 3 did not exclude it. Reproduced here exactly — 24 surviving lines — and fixed by adding --exclude for work-order.json, plan-review.json and previous-output.json, placed after the --include list because GNU grep applies those flags last-one-wins (verified: before → 24 lines, after → 0). Step 3 now states where it runs and offers the equivalent `cd _pr` form, which was also verified against a stand-in judge checkout, and states that exit 1 with empty stdout is the passing result. Step 6 keeps its sentence that the comment's mention is a hit step 3 permits, re-read against the new step 3 in the same edit. The technical finding is unchanged and was re-measured from scratch in this run: 76 changed lines in the describe-block diff, zero of them containing an assertion; 7/3 split identical in both files; fixture md5-identical; line numbers and the vitest glob re-read. The v1 and v2 fixes are kept intact — the comparison lives in exactly one artefact, the release note is one sentence by repo convention, and files[1] quotes the comment verbatim so AC-2 and files[1] cannot disagree.
residual_risks: The AC-1 and AC-5 test-count deltas are the only claims here not directly executed, because this checkout has no node_modules state and vitest cannot start. Both are stated as measurements to take against main, not as results.
